papers.summary: Defines behavioral compression rate as the smallest serialized LoRA adapter retaining a fixed fraction of held-out fine-tuning gain. The measured rate depends on both dataset and frozen base model; its proposed shrinkability predictor remains retrospectively validated.
papers.relevance: Directly informs how to measure useful low-rank compressibility rather than relying on adapter rank or reconstruction error.

evidence.quote: the smallest serialized size of a compressed adapter that, once reloaded into the frozen base model, retains a fixed fraction of its held-out fine-tuning gain
We therefore interpret Equation 7 as a retrospective empirical approximation rather than a prospectively validated prediction law.

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Compares LoRA spectra and subspaces during supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Controlled intermediate settings identify group-mean baseline subtraction as a source of their differing dynamics.
papers.relevance: Closely matches the interest in singular-value dynamics and stage-specific LoRA optimization.

evidence.quote: both contrasts appear only once a group-mean baseline is subtracted from the reward
Both configurations achieve the highest reported mean accuracy in most evaluated settings.

papers.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

papers.summary: GEAR uses normal-space spectral information to decide when a LoRA update should gain rank. Its reported LLaMA3-8B commonsense score rises from 86.61 to 88.45 while trainable parameters fall from 42.0M to 14.4M; rank audits add computation.
papers.relevance: Addresses which task-relevant directions factor gradients cannot access and how to expand a low-rank parameterization.

evidence.quote: their unobservable subspace coincides with the normal space of the low-rank manifold
On LLaMA3-8B, it raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M.
The main audit overhead therefore comes from the additional backward probes and candidate forward evaluations rather than large-scale matrix operations.

papers.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA

papers.summary: Formulates forward-only LLM fine-tuning on fixed-rank matrix manifolds. On an OPT-13B SQuAD profile, ZO-RGD and LOZO both use about 39.4 GB peak reserved memory, but ZO-RGD takes 3.51 versus 1.93 seconds per update.
papers.relevance: Connects low-rank optimization geometry to measured memory–runtime tradeoffs in LLM fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: constrain each additive update block to a fixed-rank matrix manifold while keeping the pretrained weights frozen
ZO-RGD/ZO-RGD-S average 3.51 / 3.54 seconds per update versus LOZO’s 1.93, all at approximately 39.4 GB peak reserved memory

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning

papers.summary: Develops distributed Muon-style spectral optimization with finite Newton–Schulz and low-rank communication variants. In its CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 experiment, rank-32 compression reduces simulated communication payload by 40.5% while lowering accuracy relative to the full-rank variant.
papers.relevance: Addresses spectral optimization and the communication–quality tradeoff, though the reported experiments do not establish LLM-scale performance.

evidence.quote: rank- 32 32 compression reduces the simulated communication payload by 40.5 % 40.5\% , from 385.39 to 229.34 GB
DisMUSE-LR and DisMUSE-Hybrid achieve test accuracies of 85.08% and 85.03%, respectively, illustrating the accuracy–communication trade-off.
We evaluate DisMUSE on image classification tasks

papers.title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee

papers.summary: Studies information-based measures of label-noise memorization across MNIST runs. Its memorization term rises on training samples but remains near zero on held-out samples with freshly drawn noisy labels; conclusions are limited to small image datasets and synthetic noise.
papers.relevance: Directly matches the interest in distinguishing memorization from generalization under label noise.

evidence.quote: the normalized memorization term rose with M on the training set, stayed near zero on held-out samples with freshly drawn noisy labels
The study used one architecture, a multilayer perceptron, and two small image datasets. It considered only synthetic class-conditional noise

papers.title: An Information Budget for Label-Noise Memorization, and What Statistical Complexity Tracks: A Study with Multilayer Perceptrons

papers.summary: CORE combines passage-level retrieval, snippet selection, and context management in a training-free research-agent harness. In controlled closed-search comparisons, it reports higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than two comparator harnesses across three models and benchmarks.
papers.relevance: Provides directly applicable ideas for retrieval and context handling in a handwritten research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: CORE searches at the passage level but returns evidence at the snippet level.
Across three agent models and three benchmarks, CORE achieves higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research
